item.title: 0.88.0-beta.3
item.description:
# What's New in TablePro 0.88.0-beta.3
### Added
- Share a query, a saved query or a result as a link anyone can open in a browser. ([#4253](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4253)) - Share Result masks columns that look sensitive before upload, and lets you keep, mask or remove each column. ([#4253](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4253)) - Open a shared link in TablePro to get its SQL in a new query tab, without running it. ([#4253](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4253)) - Select several rows on iPhone and iPad to export, copy or delete them. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - Import CSV, JSON and XLSX files into a table, and run SQL files, on iPhone and iPad. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - Export tables, query results, selected rows or a whole database to a file on iPhone and iPad. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - Drag an editor tab onto another window of the same connection to move it there. ([#4323](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4323)) - Name a query tab by double-clicking it or choosing Rename Tab, and the name stays after a restart. ([#4343](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4343)) - Open a cell's value editor from its context menu, the Query menu, or Option-Return. ([#4374](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4374)) - Double-click a PHP serialized value in a read-only result to open it in the viewer. ([#4377](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4377)) - Wrap Text in the data grid shows long values on several lines, up to 10 lines a row. ([#4378](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4378))
### Changed
- Typing in the query editor no longer redraws the tab strip and the rest of the window on every keystroke. ([#4286](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4286)) - Restore Dump's database picker shows favorite databases and their menu, like the toolbar switcher. ([#4303](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4303)) - The editor tab bar now scrolls, animates and drags like the macOS tab bar. ([#4323](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4323)) - Fetch All on PostgreSQL uses less memory, and binary columns load much faster. ([#4328](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4328)) - TLS connections to PostgreSQL 17 and later skip a round trip once the server is known. ([#4328](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4328)) - PostgreSQL connections open faster and a table's columns load in one round trip. ([#4328](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4328)) - Row totals stay in place while you page through a table, until you refresh or change the filters. ([#4330](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4330)) - Spanner, Cloudflare D1 and SurrealDB tables are counted only when you choose Count Exactly. ([#4330](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4330)) - SSH tunnels transfer large results many times faster over high-latency connections. ([#4331](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4331)) - libSQL queries stop at the row limit instead of downloading the whole result first. ([#4331](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4331)) - Snowflake table columns and details load without a running warehouse. ([#4331](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4331)) - Oracle results that stream in fetch 1,000 rows per round trip instead of 50. ([#4331](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4331)) - Large ClickHouse results decode about 2.7 times faster. ([#4331](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4331)) - Elasticsearch deep pages no longer download the documents they skip. ([#4332](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4332)) - Memcached key browsing reads a page of values in one request. ([#4332](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4332)) - Redis key browsing loads a page in fewer round trips on databases with 10,000 keys or more. ([#4332](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4332)) - MongoDB collection pages load without an extra round trip to the server. ([#4332](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4332)) - CSV and JSON exports of large tables finish several times faster. ([#4333](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4333)) - Refreshing a database with thousands of tables now updates only the sidebar rows that changed. ([#4334](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4334)) - VoiceOver reads the data grid columns on screen, and scrolling sideways brings in the next ones. ([#4335](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4335)) - Opening a table redraws the data grid once instead of several times. ([#4335](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4335)) - Selecting hundreds of thousands of rows in the data grid stays responsive. ([#4335](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4335)) - Wide tables and long values draw and scroll faster in the data grid. ([#4335](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4335)) - Large results use less memory, and the first edit in one no longer pauses to copy every row. ([#4340](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4340)) - Typing on a long line with line wrapping off no longer lays out every visible line again. ([#4340](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4340)) - Typing in a very large SQL file no longer pauses while syntax highlighting catches up. ([#4340](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4340)) - ROW_COUNT() and SHOW WARNINGS on MySQL and MariaDB answer for your last statement, not for a database switch. ([#4341](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4341)) - A MySQL or MariaDB query with a row limit sends the limit together with the query. ([#4341](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4341)) - MySQL and MariaDB no longer switch database before each statement, so paging and running queries take half the time. ([#4341](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4341)) - Opening a MySQL or MariaDB table reads its columns in one round trip. ([#4341](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4341)) - PostgreSQL and SQL Server results take less CPU to read. ([#4342](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4342)) - Table tabs open sorted by their primary key unless you chose another default row sort. ([#4344](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4344)) - The first page of a Kafka topic loads with one request per broker instead of one per partition. ([#4349](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4349)) - Cassandra table pages after the first load without preparing the query again. ([#4349](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4349)) - The Data Dictionary export reads a PostgreSQL schema's columns, keys and indexes in one pass, not table by table. ([#4350](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4350)) - BigQuery statements that finish within two seconds return in one request, without the half-second wait each one had. ([#4352](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4352)) - DuckDB connections now refuse SET threads below the number of processors. ([#4354](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4354)) - A PostgreSQL SQL export reads each schema's indexes, comments, sequences and enum types in one pass, not table by table. ([#4355](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4355)) - A PostgreSQL SQL import with Wrap in transaction on sends its writes in batches, not one statement at a time. ([#4356](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4356)) - A PostgreSQL SQL import stops at a statement read before an earlier write changed standard_conforming_strings. ([#4356](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4356)) - Tables open a round trip sooner from the columns read with the schema, and a bar offers Reload if they changed since. ([#4357](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4357))
### Removed
- Removed the setting that wrapped editor tabs onto more rows. ([#4323](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4323))
### Fixed
- Switching tabs cleared the undo history of grid edits still waiting to be saved. ([#4283](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4283)) - One connection TablePro could not read emptied the whole connection list and blocked saving. ([#4283](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4283)) - After a reconnect lost a transaction, a grid save used up the warning meant for your next statement. ([#4283](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4283)) - Choosing Save when closing a tab could save another tab instead if the selection changed while the prompt was up. ([#4286](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4286)) - Query History saved the statements of a script without their schema, so reopening one ran in the default schema. ([#4286](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4286)) - Query Insights grouped statements without the engine's quoting and comment rules, such as PostgreSQL's `'C:\'`. ([#4289](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4289)) - Importing a SQL file joined the words around a dropped comment, so `a/* x */FROM t` ran as `aFROM t`. ([#4289](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4289)) - Importing a SQL file split a PostgreSQL `E'...'` string continued on the next line, or a SQLite `$name(...)` parameter. ([#4289](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4289)) - The editor flagged a bracket inside a `$$` body, a `[name]`, a MySQL `#` comment or PostgreSQL's `'C:\'` as unmatched. ([#4289](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4289)) - On iOS, a ROLLBACK after a MySQL `#` comment or a nested PostgreSQL comment left the transaction shown as open. ([#4289](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4289)) - Renaming a SQL Server column failed, or renamed the wrong one, when a schema or table name held a dot or a bracket. ([#4294](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4294)) - XLSX export dropped leading and trailing spaces in text cells. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - SQLite SQL exports dropped NUL characters inside text. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - SQL exports wrote wrong trigger or routine drops for Cassandra, Teradata, SQL Server aggregates and DuckDB macros. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - Oracle triggers were left out of SQL exports, and Oracle drops failed to restore before 23ai. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - An XLSX file with one huge shared string could use up memory while it was previewed. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - A SQL export of query results failed with Read every table at one snapshot turned on. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - CSV, JSON and XLSX import was offered for MongoDB and then failed. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - Inserting a row of only defaults on Oracle did nothing on iPhone and iPad. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - Copy as SQL INSERT on iPhone and iPad quoted MySQL BIT values and listed generated columns. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - A small SQL file whose last characters were Latin-1 was read as UTF-8. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - Stopping an XLSX or Markdown export after its last row still saved the file. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - SQL exports with Drop wrote DROP ROUTINE, which no database accepts, and dropped PostgreSQL procedures as functions. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - SQL exports from two windows at once could leave out sequences and mix up their warnings. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - Markdown export cut emoji and dropped accents in aligned columns. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - PostgreSQL booleans showed as t and f on iPhone and iPad. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - A Claude, Gemini, OpenAI or xAI reply that ended with nothing in it showed an empty message instead of an error. ([#4317](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4317)) - PostgreSQL pages of a large table with no sort order no longer skip rows. ([#4328](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4328)) - Paging through a table without a primary key no longer rereads its structure on every page. ([#4330](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4330)) - Views and tables with no row estimate no longer run a full row count when you open them. ([#4330](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4330)) - Clicking another table no longer waits for the previous table's structure to finish loading. ([#4330](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4330)) - Snowflake clustering keys no longer come from a table whose name differs only by case. ([#4331](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4331)) - Parquet exports of large tables no longer take most of the memory on your Mac. ([#4333](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4333)) - On iPhone and iPad, one connection, group or tag the app could not read emptied the library and blocked changes. ([#4339](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4339)) - After a dropped MySQL connection, a read could rerun on the wrong database when USE was typed without a space. ([#4341](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4341)) - Opening a new tab crashed when another tab was titled Query 9223372036854775807. ([#4343](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4343)) - A saved or shared tab titled Query 2 was renumbered when moved to another connection or restored. ([#4343](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4343)) - Renaming a database or schema replaced the SQL in a query tab whose last run read a table there. ([#4343](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4343)) - After renaming a table or schema, the tab and the window title showed different names. ([#4343](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4343)) - Tabs such as ER Diagram kept their old language after you changed the app's language. ([#4343](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4343)) - A reopened tab could share its Query number with another open tab. ([#4343](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4343)) - A tab saved with Save As showed its file name without the extension, unlike the same file opened later. ([#4343](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4343)) - After a COMMIT, autocomplete offered no columns before FROM until it read them again. ([#4344](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4344)) - A saved connection the app could not read was replaced by its iCloud copy, or stayed after being deleted elsewhere. ([#4345](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4345)) - In Vim mode, marks stayed where they were when lines were typed, pasted or undone above them. ([#4347](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4347)) - In Vim mode, `cw`, `cj`, `dF` and `db` at the start of a line changed more text than Vim does. ([#4347](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4347)) - In Vim mode, `a` and `p` on an empty line put the text on the next line. ([#4347](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4347)) - In Vim mode, `"a2p` pasted register a once and then the last yank, and `2P` mixed up the copies. ([#4347](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4347)) - In Vim mode, `d%`, `c%`, `dn`, `d}`, `d'a` and other motions after an operator only moved the cursor. ([#4347](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4347)) - In Vim mode, Escape or leaving the command line kept a pending `d` or `c`, so the next key could delete text. ([#4347](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4347)) - In Vim mode, `ip` dropped the last character of the last paragraph. ([#4347](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4347)) - In Vim mode, Enter, `+` and `-` did nothing in Normal mode. ([#4347](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4347)) - In Vim mode, `w` stopped on a symbol followed by a variation selector, such as ❤️. ([#4347](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4347)) - In Vim mode, the next motion after `viw` shrank the selection instead of extending it. ([#4347](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4347)) - A PostgreSQL dump of a table using one enum type in two columns listed each label twice, so its CREATE TYPE failed. ([#4355](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4355)) - A SQL export or Data Dictionary dropped or mixed up tables and schemas whose names differ only in Unicode form. ([#4359](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4359)) - A DuckDB SET or table function that calls nextval() no longer breaks the connection until it is reopened. ([#4364](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4364)) - A SQL export dropped values or mixed up keys when two tables, columns or keys had names differing only in Unicode form. ([#4365](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4365)) - The ER diagram, sidebar, autocomplete and compare merged tables or schemas named alike in two Unicode forms. ([#4366](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4366)) - Pressing Return or typing on a checkbox cell opened a text field over the checkbox. ([#4374](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4374)) - A Windows path or other text that only starts like a PHP token was shown as an invalid PHP value. ([#4377](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4377)) - Remote libSQL and Turso queries lost binary values on reads or failed to send them as parameters by @shuvroroy. ([#4379](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4379)) - SQL export wrote binary values Redshift and KingbaseES restored as the wrong bytes. ([#4381](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4381)) - Cross-engine Table Transfer and Data Sync wrote booleans, dates and arrays the target engine stored wrong. ([#4381](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4381)) - A sqlite:// or duckdb:// link read its parameters, such as name, as part of the file path. ([#4390](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4390)) - Exporting tables from a SQLite file suggested the database file's full path as the file name. ([#4390](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4390)) - The SQL editor showed a restored tab or an opened SQL file without syntax colors. ([#4392](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4392)) - A query edited past 2,000,000 characters kept stale syntax colors instead of turning plain text. ([#4392](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4392)) - Read-Only Safe Mode blocked reading rows from BigQuery, Spanner, Elasticsearch, Typesense and etcd. ([#4397](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4397)) - A tab dragged out of the tab bar while TablePro was busy stuck to the pointer or fell back into the bar. ([#4403](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4403))
### Security
- Opening or browsing a DuckDB file with deeply nested constraints, defaults or views could crash the app. ([#4293](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4293)) - Attaching a DuckDB file with deeply nested constraints, defaults or views could crash the app. ([#4354](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4354))
[View release notes](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/releases/tag/v0.88.0-beta.3)

([#4356](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4356)) - A PostgreSQL SQL import stops at a statement read before an earlier write changed standard_conforming_strings. ([#4356](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4356)) - Tables open a round trip sooner from the columns read with the schema, and a bar offers Reload if they changed since. ([#4357](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4357))
### Removed
- Removed the setting that wrapped editor tabs onto more rows. ([#4323](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4323))
### Fixed
- Switching tabs cleared the undo history of grid edits still waiting to be saved. ([#4283](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4283)) - One connection TablePro could not read emptied the whole connection list and blocked saving. ([#4283](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4283)) - After a reconnect lost a transaction, a grid save used up the warning meant for your next statement. ([#4283](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4283)) - Choosing Save when closing a tab could save another tab instead if the selection changed while the prompt was up. ([#4286](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4286)) - Query History saved the statements of a script without their schema, so reopening one ran in the default schema. ([#4286](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4286)) - Query Insights grouped statements without the engine's quoting and comment rules, such as PostgreSQL's `'C:\'`. ([#4289](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4289)) - Importing a SQL file joined the words around a dropped comment, so `a/* x */FROM t` ran as `aFROM t`. ([#4289](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4289)) - Importing a SQL file split a PostgreSQL `E'...'` string continued on the next line, or a SQLite `$name(...)` parameter. ([#4289](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4289)) - The editor flagged a bracket inside a `$$` body, a `[name]`, a MySQL `#` comment or PostgreSQL's `'C:\'` as unmatched. ([#4289](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4289)) - On iOS, a ROLLBACK after a MySQL `#` comment or a nested PostgreSQL comment left the transaction shown as open. ([#4289](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4289)) - Renaming a SQL Server column failed, or renamed the wrong one, when a schema or table name held a dot or a bracket. ([#4294](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4294)) - XLSX export dropped leading and trailing spaces in text cells. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - SQLite SQL exports dropped NUL characters inside text. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - SQL exports wrote wrong trigger or routine drops for Cassandra, Teradata, SQL Server aggregates and DuckDB macros. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - Oracle triggers were left out of SQL exports, and Oracle drops failed to restore before 23ai. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - An XLSX file with one huge shared string could use up memory while it was previewed. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - A SQL export of query results failed with Read every table at one snapshot turned on. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - CSV, JSON and XLSX import was offered for MongoDB and then failed. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - Inserting a row of only defaults on Oracle did nothing on iPhone and iPad. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - Copy as SQL INSERT on iPhone and iPad quoted MySQL BIT values and listed generated columns. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - A small SQL file whose last characters were Latin-1 was read as UTF-8. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - Stopping an XLSX or Markdown export after its last row still saved the file. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - SQL exports with Drop wrote DROP ROUTINE, which no database accepts, and dropped PostgreSQL procedures as functions. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - SQL exports from two windows at once could leave out sequences and mix up their warnings. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - Markdown export cut emoji and dropped accents in aligned columns. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - PostgreSQL booleans showed as t and f on iPhone and iPad. ([#4302](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4302)) - A Claude, Gemini, OpenAI or xAI reply that ended with nothing in it showed an empty message instead of an error. ([#4317](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4317)) - PostgreSQL pages of a large table with no sort order no longer skip rows. ([#4328](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4328)) - Paging through a table without a primary key no longer rereads its structure on every page. ([#4330](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4330)) - Views and tables with no row estimate no longer run a full row count when you open them. ([#4330](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4330)) - Clicking another table no longer waits for the previous table's structure to finish loading. ([#4330](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4330)) - Snowflake clustering keys no longer come from a table whose name differs only by case. ([#4331](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4331)) - Parquet exports of large tables no longer take most of the memory on your Mac. ([#4333](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4333)) - On iPhone and iPad, one connection, group or tag the app could not read emptied the library and blocked changes. ([#4339](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4339)) - After a dropped MySQL connection, a read could rerun on the wrong database when USE was typed without a space. ([#4341](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4341)) - Opening a new tab crashed when another tab was titled Query 9223372036854775807. ([#4343](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4343)) - A saved or shared tab titled Query 2 was renumbered when moved to another connection or restored. ([#4343](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4343)) - Renaming a database or schema replaced the SQL in a query tab whose last run read a table there. ([#4343](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4343)) - After renaming a table or schema, the tab and the window title showed different names. ([#4343](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4343)) - Tabs such as ER Diagram kept their old language after you changed the app's language. ([#4343](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4343)) - A reopened tab could share its Query number with another open tab. ([#4343](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4343)) - A tab saved with Save As showed its file name without the extension, unlike the same file opened later. ([#4343](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4343)) - After a COMMIT, autocomplete offered no columns before FROM until it read them again. ([#4344](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4344)) - A saved connection the app could not read was replaced by its iCloud copy, or stayed after being deleted elsewhere. ([#4345](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4345)) - In Vim mode, marks stayed where they were when lines were typed, pasted or undone above them. ([#4347](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4347)) - In Vim mode, `cw`, `cj`, `dF` and `db` at the start of a line changed more text than Vim does. ([#4347](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4347)) - In Vim mode, `a` and `p` on an empty line put the text on the next line. ([#4347](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4347)) - In Vim mode, `"a2p` pasted register a once and then the last yank, and `2P` mixed up the copies. ([#4347](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4347)) - In Vim mode, `d%`, `c%`, `dn`, `d}`, `d'a` and other motions after an operator only moved the cursor. ([#4347](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4347)) - In Vim mode, Escape or leaving the command line kept a pending `d` or `c`, so the next key could delete text. ([#4347](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4347)) - In Vim mode, `ip` dropped the last character of the last paragraph. ([#4347](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4347)) - In Vim mode, Enter, `+` and `-` did nothing in Normal mode. ([#4347](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4347)) - In Vim mode, `w` stopped on a symbol followed by a variation selector, such as ❤️. ([#4347](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4347)) - In Vim mode, the next motion after `viw` shrank the selection instead of extending it. ([#4347](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4347)) - A PostgreSQL dump of a table using one enum type in two columns listed each label twice, so its CREATE TYPE failed. ([#4355](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4355)) - A SQL export or Data Dictionary dropped or mixed up tables and schemas whose names differ only in Unicode form. ([#4359](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4359)) - A DuckDB SET or table function that calls nextval() no longer breaks the connection until it is reopened. ([#4364](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4364)) - A SQL export dropped values or mixed up keys when two tables, columns or keys had names differing only in Unicode form. ([#4365](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4365)) - The ER diagram, sidebar, autocomplete and compare merged tables or schemas named alike in two Unicode forms. ([#4366](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4366)) - Pressing Return or typing on a checkbox cell opened a text field over the checkbox. ([#4374](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4374)) - A Windows path or other text that only starts like a PHP token was shown as an invalid PHP value. ([#4377](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4377))
### Security
- Opening or browsing a DuckDB file with deeply nested constraints, defaults or views could crash the app. ([#4293](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4293)) - Attaching a DuckDB file with deeply nested constraints, defaults or views could crash the app. ([#4354](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4354))
[View release notes](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/releases/tag/v0.88.0-beta.2)

# What's New in TablePro 0.87.0
Read-Only and Safe Mode hold on more engines, and the AI assistant and MCP clients see only what a connection allows. A Local only connection keeps its passwords off iCloud Keychain.
The tablepro command line was rebuilt, and 21 AI clients can be set up in one click from Connect a Client.
Table Health exports its findings, remembers resolved ones and runs more checks.
Query tabs keep earlier versions of their text under File > Revert To, and Manual Commit holds a connection's changes until you commit.
The grid colors values by type, and large results, queries and startup use less time and memory on macOS and iOS.
[View full changelog](https://docs.tablepro.app/changelog)

# What's New in TablePro 0.86.0
Sign in with a TablePro account to use your plan, see your devices and sync a team library. A license key from an earlier version moves into your account the first time the app opens.
A dropped connection keeps its rows while it reconnects, with Cancel, and every surface shows the same connection state.
Imports, exports, backups, restores and transfers share one progress sheet, and Quit, Close and Disconnect ask once about work still running.
Remote DuckDB connections can go through an SSH tunnel, Cloudflare Tunnel, SOCKS proxy or tunnel command, and now require the Token instead of secrets in ~/.duckdb.
A raw SQL filter can no longer run a second statement, and a DuckDB token no longer reaches another server that a later ATTACH names.
Sending feedback from inside the app is no longer available.
[View full changelog](https://docs.tablepro.app/changelog)

# What's New in TablePro 0.85.0
Neo4j, InfluxDB 2 and 3, Qdrant, Memcached and StarRocks connections, and KingbaseES with a downloadable driver.
Two to six query results show as tabs, and the Structure tab shows columns, indexes, foreign keys and checks on one page.
Masking rules hide column values in the grid, copies, exports, the AI assistant and MCP. Table Health finds bloat and unused indexes.
Routine Debugger steps through PL/pgSQL and PL/SQL, and Live Messages watches PostgreSQL notifications, Redis channels and Kafka topics.
Imported and synced connections ask before using cloud or Kerberos sign-ins, and PostgreSQL reads ~/.pgpass only when you turn it on.
Settings > Plugins is now Settings > Extensions. A .sql-formatter.json saved by 0.83 needs exporting again with sql-formatter's key names.
[View full changelog](https://docs.tablepro.app/changelog)
